summary: Primary compile-time choice for statically analyzable Splat registrations, constructor/property injection, diagnostics, and AOT-friendly object graphs.
recommendedPatterns: Prefer generated Splat registration for compile-time-known services.
Keep registrations in one composition-root SetupIOC method.
Use constructor injection and Lazy<T> for deferred dependencies.
avoidPatterns: Do not hand-write registration factories when the generator supports the graph.
Do not use service location throughout feature code.
Do not force dynamic/plugin/open-generic registrations through a static generator.
setupSteps: Declare Register/RegisterLazySingleton calls in a statically analyzable SetupIOC flow.
Resolve analyzer diagnostics and use manual/container registration only for documented dynamic cases.
commonPitfalls: Property injection requires an accessible setter.
Cycles, duplicate interfaces, inaccessible types, and mismatched lazy registrations are diagnosed at compile time.

applicationTypes: service libraries with a static composition root
features: Analyzers and code fixes for invalid graphs
packageSelection: Use Splat.DependencyInjection.SourceGenerator as a PrivateAssets=all analyzer reference alongside Splat.
Use a container adapter/manual Splat registration only for runtime discovery, plugins, unsupported open generics, or intentional container-specific behavior.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: This generator is the primary choice over handwritten Splat factories and reflection for static graphs.
Treat analyzer errors as graph defects; do not suppress a diagnostic that can be fixed in registration or constructor/property accessibility.
compatibilityNotes: Generated registrations target Splat; constructor injection remains usable from other application code.
Dynamic assemblies and runtime plugin discovery cannot be fully generated.
migrationGuidance: Move manual Register/RegisterLazySingleton factories into a single generated SetupIOC flow in slices.
Mark the intended constructor/property only when the generator cannot infer it, then remove redundant service-locator calls from feature code.
